title: Religious Freedom
byline: by Ram Swarup · Voice of India · from a speech in New Delhi, 11 July 1978
lede: In 1978 eighty-five Unitarian Christians from the US and Europe held a seminar on religious freedom in New Delhi and asked Ram Swarup to give the Hindu view. He begins with persecution by communist states and Europe's hard-won religious freedom, which he notes was followed by missionary campaigns abroad. He then explains Hindu tolerance through its many symbols of the divine, the idea that any sincere seeker finds God, and svadharma, each person's own path. The second half compares Hinduism with Christianity and Islam on scripture, faith, revelation and how each treats outsiders.
facts: Unitarian Christians who asked for the Hindu view
parts: Hindu pluralism, then “Hinduism and Semitic religions”
note: This is a Hindu apologetic. Its portrait of Christianity and Islam is the author's own, written as a contrast, and adherents and scholars of those faiths would describe them very differently. This page summarises his argument, attributed to him.

sections.title: How Europe won religious freedom, as he tells it
items: Persecution
Crusades, heresy-hunting and, today, communist states.
Reason fights back
Reason, denied for so long, turns against faith itself.
Excesses move abroad
Europe's missionaries take their zeal to other continents.
A two-way exchange
India still learned from the encounter: imperialism “was not established by men of straw”.

sections.eyebrow: Sections 5–12 · the roots of Hindu tolerance
sections.title: Why, in his account, Hinduism tolerates
items: Sec. 6
Many symbols for God
The divine has many names and forms, so no single one need be imposed.
Sec. 7
Where there is seeking, there is God
God answers sincere seekers, whatever their creed.
Sec. 8
Not an ego-god
People make gods out of their ambitions and hatreds, then force them on others.
Svadharma
Natures differ, so paths differ, like plants in a garden with their own seasons.
Sec. 11
A pilgrimage
Seekers come from different directions by different routes.
